p: when Festus was come into the: Satan's ministers are subtle and diligent in seeking every occasion: but God who watches for his own, easily hinders all their counsels.
And when he had tarried among: We may justly avoid an injury, but not with an injury.
they could not prove: They could not prove them certainly and without undoubted reasons.
But Festus: God does not only turn aside the counsel of the wicked, but also turns it upon their own heads.

And after certain days king: Festus, without even trying to, even before kings, brings to light the wickedness of the Jews, and Paul's innocence, and in this way marvellously confirms the Church of God.
Agrippa and Bernice came unto Caesarea: This Agrippa was the son of Agrippa whose death Luke spoke of before, and Bernice was his sister.
deliver any man to die: The Romans did not used to deliver any man to be punished before, etc.

But had certain questions against him: The profane and wicked take an occasion to condemn the true doctrine, because of private controversies and contentions of men between themselves: but the truth nevertheless abides safe and sure in the meantime.

superstition: This profane man calls the Jewish religion "superstition", and that before King Agrippa, but it is no wonder: for the rulers of provinces, because of the majesty of the empire of Rome, used to think themselves better than kings.
Then Agrippa said unto Festus: That is fulfilled in Paul which the Lord had told to Ananias about him; see Ac 9:15.
lord: To Augustus. Good princes refused this name at the first, that is, to be called lords, but afterwards they allowed it, as we read of Traianus.
